aliko-dangote.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
aliko-dangote.summary: The reviewed research connects political access and industrial-policy advocacy to protection of business interests. This supports an oligarchic relationship without implying every investment or protection is corrupt.

support.text: The World Bank describes Dangote chairing the private-sector side of an industrial-policy council advocating protections and incentives that can tilt competition.
Research on Nigerian cement describes links between politically connected entrepreneurs, political finance, import licensing and protection.

counter.text: The study also examines industrial-policy performance: protection can support domestic investment. Sector policy and development goals are not themselves a corrupt bargain.
counter.source: Journal of Development Studies: alternative interpretation

aliko-dangote.limitations: Policy influence is supported more strongly than a particular illegal transaction. The placement covers the documented relationship, not all 2026 refinery developments.

carlos-slim-helu.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
carlos-slim-helu.period: Telmex privatization and subsequent historical regulation
carlos-slim-helu.summary: Historical research describes political backing and access surrounding a privatized telecom monopoly. The score concerns that historical mechanism, not a claim of unchanged present-day power.

support.text: The academic account describes Slim backing Salinas, acquiring control in Telmex privatization, and continuing to exercise political connections regarding monopoly practices under Zedillo.

counter.text: Later competition reforms imposed obligations on the predominant telecom operator; historical privilege should not be projected unchanged into the present.

carlos-slim-helu.limitations: Personal access plus a policy-protected asset is the historical rationale. This is not a current market-share estimate or a criminal finding.

charles-koch.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
charles-koch.period: Long-running political organization and regulatory agenda
charles-koch.summary: The evidence concerns an organized effort to influence policy aligned with business interests, not simply a political donation or family inheritance.
charles-koch.mechanism: Business wealth → policy network → business-aligned regulation

support.text: Academic research describes the Koch network coordinating donors, ideas and advocacy to reshape party agendas over time.
support.source: Cambridge: The Koch Network and Republican Party Extremism

support.text: The chapter examines efforts by Charles and David Koch to limit climate mitigation in connection with fossil-fuel business interests.
support.source: Oxford: Billionaires in World Politics, Economy

counter.text: Policy advocacy also reflects stated free-market beliefs. Alignment with commercial interests does not show every campaign was a purchased favor or illegal.
counter.source: TIME: Koch’s business and political philosophy

charles-koch.limitations: An editorial political-economy interpretation, not a corruption allegation. It applies to Charles’s documented role, not automatically to Julia or other heirs.

gina-rinehart.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
gina-rinehart.summary: The documented episode links mining wealth, an organized tax campaign and a policy outcome affecting the industry. The personal causal contribution is less certain than the campaign’s existence.
gina-rinehart.mechanism: Mining wealth → tax campaign → industry tax treatment

support.text: Coverage identifies Rinehart and Forrest as prominent opponents of the proposed mining super-profits tax.
The report discusses their campaign and how the reworked tax changed the position of different miners.

counter.text: The revised policy affected firms differently; sector-wide democratic lobbying is an alternative to a personalized favor. The account does not prove either individual caused the outcome.

gina-rinehart.limitations: Historical campaign only. The estimate does not assert bribery, exclusive benefits, or control of the Australian government.

peter-thiel.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
peter-thiel.period: US political relationships and government-facing business, reported 2026
peter-thiel.summary: Political access and government-dependent business overlap, but the reviewed reporting does not establish that contracts were awarded as a reward for support.
peter-thiel.mechanism: Political network ↔ government-facing business; preferential link unresolved

support.text: Reuters describes Thiel’s political ties and Palantir’s growth through government contracts.

counter.text: Palantir defended its technology and safeguards. The report establishes business and political connections, not a personal quid pro quo or an improper procurement finding.

peter-thiel.limitations: Do not read contract value as proof of favoritism. A specific preferential-benefit mechanism requires more evidence.

jeff-yass.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
jeff-yass.period: TikTok policy debate and investment exposure, 2024
jeff-yass.summary: The reviewed episode creates a plausible link between political access and an investment affected by policy. The alleged influence on Trump’s position was explicitly denied.
jeff-yass.mechanism: Political access → disputed policy protection for an investment

support.text: Reuters reported a Trump meeting with Yass, whose firm held a ByteDance stake, while Trump argued against a TikTok ban.

counter.text: Trump denied changing his position because of Yass. A meeting and parallel financial interests do not themselves establish the cause of a policy change.

jeff-yass.limitations: This is an assessment of the documented 2024 episode, not the final 2026 ownership arrangement or a finding that policy was bought.

vincent-bollore.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
vincent-bollore.period: Alleged Togo port / campaign exchange; proceedings pending in 2026
vincent-bollore.summary: A specific alleged exchange connects political campaign services and a port concession. Its causal specificity matters, but the individual criminal allegations remained for trial.

support.text: The civil-party organization describes charges concerning the Lomé port concession and the referral of Bolloré and former executives for trial. It is a party to the case, not a neutral adjudicator.

counter.text: September reporting describes a trial scheduled for December 2026 and Bolloré’s challenge against judges. A rejected plea process is not a completed conviction.

vincent-bollore.limitations: The individual’s liability is not established here. Corporate settlements and relatives’ conduct must not be substituted for personal findings.

bernard-arnault.reviewDepth: Initial source-led assessment; not independently reviewed
bernard-arnault.period: French political access and corporate policy interests, 2023–2026
bernard-arnault.summary: Reporting supports substantial access and influence, but commercial size, media ownership and lawful tax deductions do not alone establish a personalized exchange.
bernard-arnault.mechanism: Corporate resources ↔ political access; preferential exchange less established

support.text: Le Monde describes extensive political access and the public cost of tax deductions associated with the Louis Vuitton Foundation.

counter.text: The same reporting notes the law was changed to reduce the relevant deduction rate. Lawful access to a general tax measure is not equivalent to a bespoke political favor.

bernard-arnault.limitations: Access is better documented than reciprocity. Tax benefits and elite meetings should not be treated as corruption findings.
